_about: A demo scene for site/boardviz/scene.js. base: the board the frame is measured on (its part table in data/boardviz). boards: more boards placed by mating their sockets onto the base's headers (mate pairs, rot in degrees, lift in mm above the base) or by at. things: loose parts in the base board's millimeter frame (motor, supply). wires: tubes from a place to a place; a place is board.part, board.part.wayN (a terminal way) or thing.wireOut; exit and enter are offsets that leave a hole straight before the wire bends; via adds points. steps: title, text, focus (a place that gets the label), and do: a list of actions run in order: drop/lift a board, show/hide a thing, wire/unwire, switch (pos up or down), shunt (drop a jumper on), led (light or off), spin/stop a motor, view (move the camera: azimuth and elevation in radians, zoom, center [x, y, height] in the base board's millimeters). Every step is one thing the reader does in the real build; the order is the recipe's order. check: what the reader sees when the step is right, or the one test to make before going on. console: a browser tool that drives the build, kept one tap away beside the steps (href, label, note). pins: the signal table from the port's README: signal, driver board pin, LaunchPad pin, what the program does with it.
title: Brushless motor on the DRV8376EVM

things.label: Motor
things.title: Brushless motor with Hall sensors
things.text: An eight-pole 24 V motor. Three phase wires carry the drive; five thin wires bring back the Hall sensors that say where the rotor is.

things.label: Motor supply
things.title: Motor supply
things.text: 4.5 to 65 V DC into VBAT and PGND. Never the LaunchPad kit's own USB. Switch it on last.

steps.title: Start with the LaunchPad, USB-C out
steps.text: The LP-AM13E230 on the bench with no cable in. The driver board goes on before any power.

steps.title: Switches S4 and S6 to BP
steps.text: They sit between the right header and the chip, each marked BP and CAN. BP means BoosterPack: the Hall signals go up to the driver board. On CAN they go to the CAN chip instead and the motor never learns its table.

steps.title: Press the EVM onto J1 to J4
steps.text: Screw terminals pointing away from the USB-C. Its Hall-block socket covers J2 and J4, the nFAULT-side socket covers J1 and J3, with its far pin on J1 pin 1.
steps.check: The EVM sits flat with no pin showing between the boards, and its screw terminals point away from the USB-C.

steps.title: Jumper J13 on the GVDD pair
steps.text: GVDD is the driver's own 5 V. This motor's Hall sensors need 4.5 V or more, so the 3.3 V choice is too low. The jumper goes on the two pins marked GVDD, not the 3V3 pair.
steps.check: J13 covers the GVDD pair. The 3V3 pin stands alone.

steps.title: Hall wires into the green block
steps.text: Bottom to top: white HALL A, blue HALL B, green HALL C, red HALL POWER, black HALL GROUND. A Hall sensor is a small switch that flips as a rotor magnet passes it; three of them tell the program which sixth of a turn the rotor is in. A, B and C can be in any order because the program learns the table; power and ground must be right.
steps.check: Five wires in, red at the fourth terminal from the bottom, black at the top. Tug each one.

steps.title: Motor phases into the three-way terminal
steps.text: Yellow to OUT A, red to OUT B, black to OUT C. Any order works; the learn step finds the table. Leave the shaft free to turn.

steps.title: Supply into the two-way terminal
steps.text: Red to VBAT, black to PGND, supply switched off. 12 V from an adapter with the barrel cut off is the tested supply; 5 V from a cut USB cable on a 2 A charger also spins it. Keep it under 20 V for this motor. For the first power-up use a supply that limits current to about 0.5 A, or an adapter rated no higher.
steps.check: Before power: a meter between VBAT and PGND reads open, not a short, and red is on VBAT. Swapped supply wires can destroy the driver.

steps.title: USB-C in, then the supply on
steps.text: VM, AVDD and GVDD light; MCU lights when the program runs. Open the serial port at 115200, press l to learn the Hall table (the shaft clicks round six steps, about 25 s), then 2 and g to spin. In the animation the yellow dots are supply current, the blue dots the Hall signals coming back, the orange dots the drive going out.
steps.check: Three lights on and NFAULT off. If NFAULT is on, switch the supply off: a phase wire is loose or shorted, or the supply sagged. Then open the motor console or the serial port.

console.label: Open the motor console
console.note: after step 8. Connect, set a speed, Run. STOP stays on screen.
